items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had the honour of playing for him one week at the Lafayette theatre.

ctx.x: As there was a shortage of cigarettes in Japan and we were allowed to buy a certain amount of cartons a week from the P.X.(post exchange), there was no end to the wonderful Japanese souvenirs we could have in exchange for a few cartons of cigarettes. I bought many nice silk typical robes and other souvenirs for my family and special friends back home. I had also acquired quite a few from the Philippines because the same conditions existed concerning cigarettes as it was in Japan.

I met at the Honcho House, a very famous Broadway and Harlem comedian who did a one man show act. His name was Johnny Huggins, and I had seen his act many times, and had the honour of playing for him one week at the Lafayette theatre. Everyone that knew Johnny called him "Banjo", because he used the word in association with almost any conversation he had on any subject. If he disliked something, he would say: that banjo is out of tune, the strings are broken, or it sounds bad, and many other expressions…
